panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Panel A is an axial CT scan clearly showing duodenal compression and reduced aortomesenteric distance, meeting all inclusion criteria for SMAS. B: Panel B is a sagittal CT reconstruction explicitly showing a reduced aortomesenteric angle, which is a characteristic finding of SMAS. C: Panel C is a coronal CT reconstruction showing characteristic gastric and proximal duodenal dilatation resulting from obstruction in SMAS. D: Panel D illustrates an associated finding (renal vein compression) within the narrowed SMAS space. While not a defined finding key, the context links it to SMAS pathophysiology. E: Panel E demonstrates SMAS findings in a context of cachexia, specifically showing narrowing and dilatation. F: Panel F shows a chronic presentation of SMAS, characterized by reduced distance and duodenal dilatation.

(B) Sagittal CT reconstruction showing a markedly reduced aortomesenteric angle of 10°. (C) Coronal CT reconstruction demonstrating marked gastric and proximal duodenal dilatation proximal to the site of compression. (D) Associated Nutcracker phenomenon, with compression of the left renal vein within the narrowed aortomesenteric space. (F) Chronic presentation with reduced aortomesenteric distance and less pronounced proximal dilatation.
